source.title: On the Lipschitz Constant of Deep Networks and Double Descent
source.authors: Matteo Gamba; Hossein Azizpour; Mårten Björkman

record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly reproduces model-wise double-descent test-error curves, using width sweeps and test error, while also extending the experiments to additional architectures and measures.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own test-error sweeps over model size and epochs, plus its empirical-Lipschitz results relevant to effective complexity. Cited results from other work are not recorded. Most plotted values are not numerically tabulated.
record.test_reason: The paper reproduces model-wise double descent in test error with Nakkiran-style width sweeps (ω=1..64, label noise, no explicit regularization). It reports epoch-wise test-error behaviour by width group. Its main contribution is correlates of double descent (Lipschitz constant, curvature, distance from initialization), and these do not map onto a claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report that the empirical Lipschitz constant, loss curvature and distance from initialization are non-monotonic in width and correlate with test-error double descent. They propose curvature and distance from initialization as factors controlling optimization and function complexity. The evidence is correlational, and they call the true latent factors an open problem.
record.recipe_differences: Uses width sweeps and test error to reproduce double descent, but studies additional architecture families and focuses extensively on empirical Lipschitz measures; its settings are not the original paper's exact settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior varies with model width and training time; experiments also vary architecture, dataset, and label-noise setting. For epoch-wise results, the pattern differs across small, near-threshold, and large models.

fits_no_version.finding: Empirical Lipschitz constant (and an upper bound, Fig. 2) rises to a peak near the interpolation threshold and then falls with width. It correlates with test error and also holds on test and random-noise inputs (Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-space smoothness of trained networks is non-monotonic in model size and tracks model-wise double descent.

fits_no_version.finding: Across epochs the Lipschitz constant increases monotonically for all widths. Its growth rate varies with width and is said to correlate with epoch-wise test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lipschitz growth rate over training correlates with epoch-wise double descent.

fits_no_version.finding: Hessian trace, largest and smallest Hessian eigenvalues, SGD noise-covariance top eigenvalue, and per-layer distance from initialization all peak near the interpolation threshold (Figs. 3, 5, 7, 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-landscape curvature and distance from initialization are non-monotonic in width and peak at the interpolation threshold.

record.problems: The test-error and Lipschitz results are primarily figures without tabulated numerical values. The reported epoch-wise test-error shape depends on width: small models plateau and near-threshold models worsen during prolonged training, whereas the authors describe epoch-wise double descent for large models. No uncertainty intervals or significance tests are reported in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Only deep networks are tested; no non-neural model classes. The U-shape before the threshold is only stated in passing for deep nets.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epochs and samples. The Lipschitz constant is a correlate.
Noise levels are shown, but the peak's dependence on noise is not analysed. No regularization sweep (all models are trained without explicit regularization). No multiple peaks.

missing.what: Curvature, noise-covariance and distance-from-initialization curves versus width (correlates; relevant to fits_no_version, not to a version)

record.verdict_notes: Double descent is reproduced as the setting for correlate analysis. Seeds are 3 for ConvNets and 5 for ResNets, but no error bars are reported. V4 and V6 links were removed from the test-error rows: all systems are deep nets, and noise is not analysed as a driver.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests width/model-size sweeps in its stated vision and machine-translation settings; it does not test every model class or setting.
Epoch-wise test-error behavior is reported for ConvNets and ResNet18s on CIFAR-10 with 20% noisy labels, not across all architectures, datasets, noise levels, or training procedures.
No sweep over the number of training samples near the interpolation threshold is reported.

The tested classes are neural-network architecture families (ConvNets, ResNet18s, Vision Transformers, and Transformers); non-neural model classes and a general account subsuming classical U-shaped curves are not tested.

The paper measures empirical Lipschitz behavior against model size and training time, but does not test a single effective-complexity measure across model size, epochs, and sample size; sample size is not varied.
Label-noise settings are varied, but the study does not establish that noise causes the peak. It does not test multiple/triple peaks or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
The paper does not re-express complexity using an effective parameter count or test whether that yields an ordinary U-shaped curve.
